mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the discount rate applied to future equity cash flows, lowering the present value of expected dividends and earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day ahead returns in such regimes are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) in a 5-year walk-forward test.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 3% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 anticipates a policy tightening cycle, causing a sharp decline in equity valuations and negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 3% and remains above for 2 months
failure_condition: In regimes with actual policy rate cuts within 6 months, 20-day returns do not turn negative as predicted.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly PAYEMS (labor market activity) accompanied by a concurrent decline in UNRATE (unemployment) suggests a tight labor market, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% month-over-month while UNRATE decreases by >0.5 percentage points
failure_condition: In samples with structural unemployment shocks, the interaction signal does not predict 5-day returns (R-squared < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in GDPC1 (real private consumption) of at least 3% for two consecutive months indicates strong consumer demand, which elevates earnings growth forecasts and produces positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 grows by >=3% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In recessions with inverted yield curves, the signal fails to predict positive 20-day returns (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO (industrial production) by more than 5% in two consecutive months signals supply-side weakness, prompting equity market sell-off and negative 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by >5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: During periods of simultaneous demand expansion and no policy tightening, the signal does not yield statistically significant negative returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 1% for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 expects accommodative policy to persist, amplifying risk appetite and producing positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS stays below 1% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: In post-crisis normalization phases, the signal fails to predict returns when yield curve steepens sharply (10y-2y spread > 100 bps).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in UNRATE below 4% combined with a decline in HOUST (housing starts) below 1,000K suggests a softening labor market and housing market, which can depress growth expectations and drive negative 5-day S&P 500 returns.
regime_hint: labor market softening and housing weakness
failure_condition: During periods of simultaneous fiscal stimulus and low unemployment, the interaction does not predict negative returns (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A statistically significant positive cross-correlation (lag 1) between S&P 500 20-day returns and a composite of all candidate proxies (GDPC1, FEDFUNDS, CPIAUCSL) indicates a general macroeconomic momentum effect that drives positive returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: In out-of-sample tests across multiple regimes, the composite signal explains less variance in returns than the best single proxy (R-squared < 0.02).
